definitions.explanation: Selfish attitude or behavior that prioritizes one's own desires over others. From English 'ego.' Carries a strongly negative connotation in Japanese, closer to 'selfishness' than the neutral psychological sense.

examples.japanese: {親|おや}のエゴを{子|こ}どもに{押|お}し{付|つ}けるな。
examples.english: Don't force your parental ego on your children.

examples.japanese: {環境|かんきょう}{保護|ほご}を{訴|うった}えながら{車|くるま}に{乗|の}るのは、エゴではないかと{言|い}われた。
examples.english: I was told that driving a car while advocating for environmental protection is hypocritical selfishness.

notes:
Borrowed from English 'ego,' but in Japanese this word almost always carries a negative connotation of selfishness — it is rarely used in the neutral psychological or philosophical sense. When Japanese speakers say エゴ, they typically mean someone is acting selfishly or imposing their own desires.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- エゴを{通|とお}す: to push through one's selfish desires
- エゴを{押|お}し{付|つ}ける: to force one's selfishness on others
- {親|おや}のエゴ: parental selfishness
- エゴイスト: egoist; selfish person
- エゴイズム: egoism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {我|わ}がまま: selfishness; willfulness — more colloquial and broader in usage, common in everyday speech
- {自己中|じこちゅう}: self-centered (abbreviation of {自己中心的|じこちゅうしんてき}) — casual/slang, very common among younger speakers
- {利己的|りこてき}: selfish; self-interested — more formal and literary
